A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiFoley work. The main text, equations, Figures 1–6, Tables 1–7, and Appendices A.1–A.3 support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original audio-generation experiments, controlled-Foley evaluations, a human study, and ablations, including the guidance-scale results in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results, human evaluation, and main-text and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The DiT/DAC-VAE architecture, multimodal conditioning, quality tags, masked training, and inference procedures are unchanged. Section 3.2's added wording about pairing simultaneous audio and video features explains the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain VGGSound and HQ-SFX training, VGGSound/VGGSound-Sync and Greatest-Hits evaluations, and Adobe Audition reference audio for FAD. The generation, text-control, audio-visual-control, extension, and quality-control scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparison methods and FoleyCrafter variants. Table 1's DAC-VAE (VGGSound) label identifies the existing reconstruction oracle. MMAudio is newly cited but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Test subsets, sample durations and counts, training budgets, guidance settings, metrics, and human-study procedures are retained. The added statement that VGGish-based FAD uses 16 kHz audio documents an existing evaluation without reporting a change from a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The negative-prompting comparisons, conditioning analyses, fine-tuning and no-text ablations, quality-control examples, and Appendix A.2 guidance-scale analysis are unchanged. No robustness test or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains 95% confidence intervals, p-values below 10^-20, and N = 400 with 20 participants. Sampling and random-selection information in Appendix A.3 is unchanged; no new seed or repeated-run reporting appears.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains MultiFoley's CLAP score of 34.4 and AV-Sync of 0.80 seconds; Table 3 retains the overall win rate of 90.2% with a ±2.9 interval. Table 7's guidance-scale results also match.

T1.justification: The conditional diffusion formulation and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about multimodal control, joint training, 48 kHz generation, and empirical performance. Adding 'via language as bridges' to a contribution bullet restates the language supervision already described in v3.

C2.justification: The expanded wording about quality tags and dataset distributions reiterates the explanation already present in v3 Sections 3.2 and 4.4. Interpretations of synchronization, semantic control, and FAD tradeoffs, together with Section 5's dataset and multiple-event limitations, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies that VGGish-based FAD operates on 16 kHz audio, supplying a previously unstated evaluation detail. Architecture and training details in Appendix A.1, study documentation, and access links are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds MMAudio and its reference, acknowledging concurrent joint video-to-audio and text-to-audio training across datasets. The existing distinction based on MultiFoley's richer controls now follows this discussion. All previously cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Short passages clarify language supervision, temporal feature pairing, quality tags, and evaluation references. The human-study introduction is shortened and a grammatical omission is corrected. The section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 adds the VGGSound qualifier to the oracle label. Table 3 moves from the left to the right column on page 7, shifting Table 4 downward. Reference spillover creates a mostly empty page 13 and moves the appendices back one page; all six figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Specifying the 16 kHz FAD input rate improves evaluation transparency, while acknowledging MMAudio makes the research positioning more complete. These are limited gains because the method and empirical evidence, including the appendices, are unchanged. The mostly empty reference continuation page is a small layout cost.
